craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of scrutiny vindicated; vyabhicāri utsāha at shining exception. Sanskrit-first: amarśita (UNSCRUTINIZED — kept; sterility named); marśana-vidhi elision + asau force per UNC (held open, not filled). Rows: 9 (knows-nothing/is-nothing/no-grasping/no-gain — sterility hammered), 1 (‘always’ closes — bliss-duration last). Close: ‘bliss in Your hymn always’. Rupture: semicolon (sterility turns to shining — antithesis hinged). Rejected: filling elision — killed by UNC; ‘fruit’ for gain — killed: gain gains; ‘sap’ glossed — killed: one-sap kept (eka-rasa technical). Read aloud: un-SCRU-tin-ized, the-SELF knows-NO-thing, IS-no-thing … BUT-ŚI-va, SELF-shin-ing, ONE-sap OF-all — HENCE-bliss IN-your-HYMN al-WAYS.

lines: Unscrutinized, the self knows nothing, is nothing — no grasping, no gain;
but Śiva, self shining, one sap of all — hence bliss in Your hymn always.
l4.sanskrit_cite: anāmṛṣṭaḥ svātmā na hi bhavati bhāvapramitibhāj | śivaś cāsau svātmā sphurad akhilabhāvaikasarasas

reads_against.argmap: What if the self goes unscrutinized? → Unscrutinized, no knowing; scrutinized, Śiva shining one-sapped — bliss.
c1_essence: Unscrutinized sterility vs shining Śiva one-sapped: bliss follows scrutiny.
